correctness.rationale: Dual reconstruction and two Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities give \(1\le\sqrt{E(S-E)}\) for every unit vector and every weave. Solving the resulting quadratic is valid because duality forces \(B_\Lambda B_\Gamma\ge1\) and hence \(S\ge2\). The sharpness construction realizes a two-by-two positive matrix with trace \(S\) and determinant \(1\), so its smaller eigenvalue is exactly the claimed constant; converting its eigenbasis into the two index coordinates gives a real one-dimensional dual pair attaining equality.

value.rationale: The result sharpens a standard robustness guarantee under exactly the same dual g-frame hypotheses and determines the best possible lower constant from the two natural Bessel conditioning parameters. Equality examples exist for every admissible parameter pair and already occur in dimension one with two indices, showing that the constant reflects a genuine extremal boundary rather than an artifact of proof technique.
